label: Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro LTE-A CAT-6 (MAX-BR1-PRO-LTEA-W-T)
description: Peplink Pepwave MAX BR1 Pro - rugged DIN-mount single-cellular router: 1x GE WAN, 4x GE LAN, an embedded LTE-A (CAT-6) modem with redundant SIM slots, 802.11n Wi-Fi (300 Mbps) and GPS. 120 Mbps router throughput, 24 W maximum from 12-28 V DC terminal block or AC adapter, -40 to 65 C.
notes: This is the CAT-6 / LTE-A member (product code MAX-BR1-PRO-LTEA-W-T, Worldwide; the P-T code is the Asia-Pacific twin): LTE-A modem 300 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up, so `wwan0` is 300M. The datasheet gives the copper plainly - 'WAN Interface 1x GE', 'LAN Interface 4x GE' - so the 4+1 split is quoted, and the 300 Mbps Wi-Fi is 802.11a/n or b/g/n, one 2.4/5 GHz radio rather than two. One embedded modem with **redundant SIM slots**: a single cellular bearer with a standby SIM, not two modems, so a failover lab should expect one `wwan0` and a SIM switch inside it. That is why `wwan0` is a `wireless` port here - this catalogue's name for a cellular bearer, as on Balance 20X and UBR-LTE - and it cannot be cabled, which the engine enforces with `E_CONNECTOR_MISMATCH`. The ports declare `poeIn: 0`: the BR1 Pro takes 12-28 V DC on a terminal block or an AC adapter and powers nothing over Ethernet, so the access-point heuristic must not invent a draw. No CLI - management is the web UI and InControl - so no `cli` capability.
